Subject: Mutual action heatmap + decision criteria — SeniorCare / Redwood

Hi Laura / Derek —

Thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our side and a proposed next set of steps so we keep momentum:

Call highlights
- Use case: inpatient discharge notes + claims enrichment (reduce readmissions, improve coding accuracy)
- Key decision criteria you shared: latency under 300ms for summary flows, on-prem / VPC option required for PHI, vendor must provide SOC 2 Type II evidence and answers to RFI, predictable unit economics (cost-per-1k tokens)
- Initial scope: 3 pilot clinics (approx 250k tokens/day peak) with expansion if latency / accuracy targets are met

Stakeholder map (as captured)
- Economic buyer: Laura Chen (Head of Informatics) — budget owner
- Procurement lead: Derek Morales — formal contract flow and vendor checks
- Legal reviewer: Anya Singh — T&Cs and data processing language
- Security: security team (TBD, Derek said he would loop in)
- Technical champion: Dr. Ravi Patel (on your side) — will run pilot acceptance tests

Proposed MAP (draft attached: MAP_draft_v1.xlsx) — short version
- Week 0: NDA & intro to procurement (you)
- Week 1–2: Security questionnaire + SOC2 summary (we provide)
- Week 3–4: Pilot SOW + sign-off on success metrics
- Week 5–8: Pilot execution & acceptance testing
- Post-pilot: commercial negotiations / commitment

Asks / next steps
1) Can you confirm the procurement cadence — is 6–8 weeks from procurement kickoff to PO realistic? If not, what gate length should we expect?
2) Please confirm the security contact (name/email) so we can send the Security_Q_A.pdf and SOC2 summary directly.
3) Any additional hard decision criteria beyond latency / PHI controls / cost-per-token that will block procurement (e.g., specific data residency language, attestations)?

I've attached the draft MAP and our security Q&A. Marissa / Ben — assigning you below to specific owners based on the replies.

Thanks —
Sean

--
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

Subject: Re: Mutual action heatmap + decision criteria — SeniorCare / Redwood

Sean —

Great recap, and thanks for pulling that together so quickly. A few clarifications from our side:

Procurement timeline
- Typical procurement cadence is ~6–8 weeks for contracts under $250k. For anything above that threshold procurement will require an additional finance review (adds 2–4 weeks). For pilot budget we're aiming under $200k so 6–8 weeks is reasonable.

Security / legal
- Please send Security_Q_A.pdf to Derek (copied) and Anya for their review. Our security team lead is Tara Nguyen (tara.nguyen@seniorcarehealth.com) — I expect them to ask for:
  - SOC 2 Type II report (redacted ok)
  - Data processing addendum (DPA) with clear PHI handling language
  - Network architecture diagram for VPC/on-prem deployment options

Decision criteria — to be explicit
- Production latency requirement: <300ms for summary endpoints at 95th percentile
- Data handling: must support VPC/private deployment; no long-term storage of PHI unless DPA explicitly permits
- Accuracy: clinical summary F1 score target (we'll share baseline after pilot)
- Unit economics: target blended cost that keeps incremental CPAs within our run-rate expectations (procurement will ask for an estimate)

On the MAP: the timeline looks good. Two asks: 1) add an explicit procurement gate (signature of Master Services Agreement) as a milestone; 2) include an internal acceptance test owner (we'll assign Dr. Ravi).

I'll review the MAP with Derek and Anya and get back with exact procurement lead availability — happy to aim for a kickoff next week if Redwood can deliver SOC2 and network diagram by Friday.

Thanks,
Laura

--
Laura Chen
Head of Informatics, SeniorCare Health
